narrative:
The model estimates a 47% chance that you will leave your job, which is high enough for the company to deny your promotion as a precaution.

Three main factors shaped this outlook. First, your total years of experience across all jobs had the strongest influence and pulled the prediction toward staying. At 1-5 years, you are in the most common group among employees the model expects to remain, yet the pattern in the data still suggests that people at this early career stage tend to explore other options.

The second strongest factor was that you have received other job offers while working here. This pushed the prediction noticeably toward leaving. Having external opportunities often signals that someone is actively considering a move.

Third, you described balancing your work and personal life as difficult. This also nudged the outcome toward leaving. While most employees the model predicts will stay report a manageable balance, your situation stands out as more challenging.

Taken together, your solid but still limited experience, the presence of outside offers, and the strain of balancing work with life created enough concern for the system to flag a real risk of departure.

The company should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore ways to improve your work-life balance. You may want to reflect on whether the external opportunities better match what you are looking for long-term. Addressing these points now could change the outlook for both sides.
